title: Quantized serving livelock and per-model sample sensitivity remediation
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-02-09 we observed a cluster of serving incidents for several int8-quantized model variants where requests entered a livelock: generators either did not make forward progress or produced repeated token stutters leading to high latency, request retries, and apparent accuracy drift for a subset of customers running RLHF-style prompts. The incident surfaced as a capacity oscillation (autoscaler reacting to tail latency spikes) and model-level accuracy regressions in canaries.

Timeline: 2025-02-09 02:14 UTC - first spike in tail latency; 02:18 UTC - platform alerts for repeated generation loops; 02:45 UTC - mitigation: route affected customers to float32 variant; 03:10 UTC - partial rollback of quantized kernel for canary pool; 09:00 UTC - initial RCA stood up; 2025-02-10 - triage and assignment.

Root cause (summary): A race between the KV cache eviction/rehydration and a per-request fast-path in the int8 fused-attention kernel produced a rare state where the runtime would repeatedly re-execute a short suffix of tokens with stale prefix state. Contributing factors: (1) kernel variant implemented an optimization that bypassed a rehydration barrier when cache miss rates were low, (2) a retry path for transient I/O would re-submit requests without advancing an epoch tag leading to duplicated continuations, and (3) a subset of RLHF-style prompts are sample-sensitive — small numerical differences change top-k sampling and make regressions visible as accuracy drift.

Why this escaped canaries: existing canaries used long-context deterministic prompts; the failure mode affects short to medium context adversarial prompts that trigger eviction + quick rehydration. Canary coverage gap discovered.

Immediate mitigations applied: routing policy to fall back to float32 variant for affected tenant groups, raised eviction threshold for high-QPS pools to reduce rehydration frequency, emergency hotfix to add a conservative rehydration fence for the fused-attention kernel in the canary pool.

Longer-term corrective actions (see action items): epoch-based KV cache tags, deterministic fallback for repeated prefix loops (auto-fallback to float variant after N repeated continuations), broadened canary suite to include short-context adversarial prompts and stochastic sampling checks, additional telemetry for prefix replays and lifetime of per-request cache handles, rollout gating by model sensitivity score.

Acceptance criteria: no livelock regressions in staging canaries for 7 consecutive days; added telemetry shows zero prefix-replay occurrences for rolled out pools for 48 hours post-deploy; automated regression eval (seed set) shows <0.5% delta on quality metric for sensitive prompts compared to float baseline.

Notes: this ticket focuses on runtime fixes, canary coverage, and operational controls. Separate follow-ups will cover quant autotuner changes and model onboarding guidance for sample-sensitive models.

release_notes: runtime-1.20: Add epoch-tagged KV rehydration fence for int8 fused-attention kernels; auto-fallback to float variant after repeated prefix replay; expanded canary suite for short-context adversarial prompts; telemetry additions for prefix_replay_count and cache_handle_lifetime_ms.
playbook: Create a short playbook entry: detect runtime.prefix_replay_count > 0.5/hr -> immediate route-to-float variant -> raise eviction threshold for pool -> open ENG ticket to investigate model sensitivity. Playbook added to runbook repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/quant-playbook.md
